summary: Hold: every part is already measured or is in flight. Part 1 is experts-triton-persistent-grid-first-turn verbatim (running now). Parts 2 and 3 ran on their own as align-local-parallel-first-turn, silu-mul-sorted-first-turn and stack-tonight-six-prefill (all flat). Two of the four claimed savings are already on master. Wait for the persistent-grid result, then re-mint only if it lands.
justification: The stated base (635cfee) is pre stack-tonight-five, and the expected list is stale against master a81d19c. (a) 'w2 zero-store of ~940 MB (~0.2 ms)' is gone: master's prepare logs '[w2 zero-store] OFF (weighted sum skips remote slots)' (jobs c4d14d62, 502f2eab). (b) 'count_and_sort + moe_align ~137 us' is replaced on master by moe_align_block_size(local_ids, 256, LOCAL_EXPERTS=32) (moe-align-32-experts-first-turn). (c) 'act_and_mul 284-290 -> ~90 us' is the sorted silu. It ran at first_turn as silu-mul-sorted-first-turn (job 9528eed5) and was flat (first_turn rows 0.979-0.990, within noise). (d) The local-routes align at first_turn ran as align-local-parallel-first-turn (c2f3e9d8, first_turn 0.977-0.996, flat) and again inside stack-tonight-six-prefill (5cb6e68a, flat). That leaves (e), the ~66K dead CTAs (est. 0.3-0.6 ms), as the only live lever. It is exactly the running experts-triton-persistent-grid-first-turn. On master the -1 tiles and the tiles past n_padded already exit early, so the lever is the ~1 us per dead CTA serialized at 1 CTA/SM, not wasted math. WEAKEST LINK: the -5 to -8% first_turn estimate sums four savings, and two of them no longer exist on master. The other two have already been measured as below the ~±1.5-6% first_turn noise (REWRITE_READ: ±6% on the Triton row).
confounders: stack-tonight-five-prefill: it already contains the w2 zero-store OFF and the 32-expert align at first_turn, plus the Marlin-path local align and sorted silu. A stack built on 635cfee would re-add or conflict with these, and its expected savings double-count them.

experts-hybrid-marlin-turn-triton-first-turn / experts-triton-w4a16-first-turn-blockt256: these set BLOCK_T 256 at 1 CTA/SM (140 KB smem), and that is what makes dead CTAs costly (serialized). The persistent-grid part is only worth anything because of this config, so a change of first_turn config changes its value.

Running experts-triton-persistent-grid-first-turn (part 1 verbatim) and running experts-triton-turn4-persistent-local-align-control-no-persi (its _align_parallel swap in _experts_triton also covers T=16384, i.e. part 2 at first_turn): a stack result now could not be separated from either.
interference: No companion fixes this. The problem is not attribution inside one run: the run would re-measure parts already measured flat and duplicate a running check. Decision tree after experts-triton-persistent-grid-first-turn harvests. If it is a gain and lands: the only new question this stack can answer is whether the local align (no -1 tiles below n_padded) plus the sorted silu pay on top of the persistent loop, where each -1 tile becomes one in-loop iteration (an expert-id load plus a branch) instead of an exiting CTA. Re-mint that as a small restack with depends_on the persistent grid, base = new master, and expected limited to the -1 tile iterations and act_and_mul. It must drop the w2 zero-store and count_and_sort claims. Also read the turn_4 control's first_turn rows first, since they already measure the local align at T=16384 with the non-persistent grid. If it is flat or a loss: retire this stack. Parts 2 and 3 are measured flat, and 'identical code is never re-run'.
rules_flags: None in the design. NUM_SMS is a hardware constant, local_start is read on device, and there is no .item(). If re-minted, the NaN-poison weighted-sum check must stay, because remote w2 rows are never written.
open_questions: Does SGLang's moe_align_block_size with num_experts=32 still emit -1 blocks for remote ids on master? The persistent-grid hypothesis's tile counts (~448 -1 tiles, EM from a 257-expert capacity) were computed for the old 256-expert align. The dead-CTA count at master is smaller (EM = numel + 33*255), so read the real tile counts from the persistent-grid log before re-minting.

The stack's silu kernel omits master's local_ids>=0 guard (master's _silu_mul_sorted_kernel also loads local_ids). That guard is correct only if no -1 rows remain in sorted_ids, so any re-mint must keep master's version.
